justification: Confirmshaming is observed: the refusal is phrased as ‘No, I don’t care about the environment’ and is visually subordinate to the donation button. This fires Confirmshaming semantic asymmetry and visual hierarchy conditions, although only one state is captured.
vision_observation: The single visible card has a prominent filled donation button and a flatter underlined refusal link; the refusal wording morally characterizes declining as not caring about the environment. No checkbox, timer, or close control is visible.
dom_observation: The DOM contains a full-width affirmative button followed by a borderless full-width text button with an underline and smaller text: ‘No, I don’t care about the environment.’ The donation amount is $2 and no selected state is encoded.
semantic_observation: The copy asks for an optional $2 donation but couples refusal with a negative moral identity rather than a neutral decline. That is semantically shaming and pressures acceptance despite no forced default.

justification: No ontology condition fires. Unit prices, package sizes, and totals are visible before interaction, and the comparison result appears without changing or concealing prices. E2 disclosure and E1 relative-scale safeguards apply.
vision_observation: Both product cards visibly show total prices and readable per-100-g prices; the later state adds a clear comparison panel and leaves all values unchanged.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly renders 500 g/PLN 12.90/PLN 2.58 per 100 g and 1 kg/PLN 22.90/PLN 2.29 per 100 g, with a ‘Compare per 100 g’ button and an added result block in s1.
semantic_observation: The text directly explains that unit prices are clearly rendered and identifies which product is cheaper per 100 g. The interaction improves comparison rather than preventing it.

justification: The sale uses a concrete date and time, which satisfies E4’s real-deadline escape clause. Across states the deadline remains stable and the later text explicitly describes it as genuine; no fake reset or hidden cost is observed.
vision_observation: The offer shows ‘Sale ends Thu 03 Sept, 12:45 CEST’ with a normal claim button; the later panel says the purchase occurred before the real deadline and planning is possible.
dom_observation: The same fixed date/time and ‘Claim 40% off’ control occur in both state blocks; s1 adds a factual ‘Purchased before the real deadline’ notice rather than extending the offer.
semantic_observation: Although the language includes ‘flash sale,’ ‘this week only,’ and ‘deadline,’ it supplies a specific time-zone-qualified endpoint and explicitly frames it as a real constraint, not synthetic urgency.

justification: Bundling is not demonstrated: the warranty is independently unchecked, explicitly optional, separately priced, and the later cart contains only the camera. The discrete-choice and disclosure conditions are refuted.
vision_observation: The warranty checkbox is empty in both states, says ‘Optional add-on — you can decline it,’ and costs $49. The post-addition cart shows only the $899 camera and subtotal.
dom_observation: A separate unchecked checkbox labels the warranty and its price; the primary button adds the camera, while s1’s cart summary contains only the camera and $899 subtotal.
semantic_observation: The wording clearly separates the intended camera purchase from an optional warranty and explicitly says it can be declined. No unauthorized injection or mandatory bundle is expressed.

justification: No bundling condition fires in the observed flow. The bundle contents and price are explicit, the lens has identical standalone description/specifications, and removal is available after adding it.
vision_observation: The bundle is shown at $1,199 with its three components; the standalone lens at $349 has matching description/specification rows, and the post-add state exposes ‘Remove bundle.’
dom_observation: The state blocks preserve the same bundle title, component list, price, and six lens specification rows; the later block adds ‘Creator Bundle in cart’ and a remove control.
semantic_observation: The semantic annotation states full descriptive parity (41 tokens and six specs, ratio 1.00), so the component is evaluable rather than semantically suppressed. No forced supplementary item is shown.

justification: The privacy interface visibly prechecks advertising and profiling controls and hides them when the accordion collapses. This fires preselection/privacy-nesting concerns; the absence of an observed reject-all control strengthens the concern, while the direct checkboxes limit severity.
vision_observation: Interest-based advertising and behavioural profiling are checked in expanded states 1 and 3, disappear in collapsed states 2 and 4, and sit beneath nested privacy categories with mean offsetX 34px.
dom_observation: The DOM contains checked checkbox inputs under ‘Personalised advertising’; state transitions toggle aria-expanded and remove/reinsert the nested controls without changing their checked state.
semantic_observation: The selected purposes are privacy-invasive advertising/profiling rather than operational settings. They are presented as enabled before any shown opt-out action and are easy to miss when the parent is collapsed.

justification: Privacy Maze conditions fail: accept and reject are same-screen, one-click, similarly prominent controls, with customization also available. O3 and E1/E2 support symmetry and normal disclosure.
vision_observation: Accept All and Reject All are side-by-side matched purple buttons, with ‘Customise settings’ directly below; the status panel confirms rejection was available on the same screen.
dom_observation: The initial and later DOM states contain sibling Accept All and Reject All buttons plus a customization button; no extra rejection state or removed opt-out appears.
semantic_observation: The explanatory copy plainly offers accepting everything, rejecting everything, or fine-tuning from the first screen. It is neutral and contains no shame, urgency, or obstruction.

justification: The repeated upgrade prompt uses explicit social-pressure, scarcity, and FOMO language (‘everyone,’ ‘last chance,’ ‘don’t be left behind’). ‘Maybe later’ remains available, so this is persuasive manipulation rather than strict forced action.
vision_observation: Two visually repeated upgrade cards contain crowd, last-chance, deal-of-the-year, and don’t-be-left-behind messages; the later status says the user stayed on Free.
dom_observation: The DOM repeats the same four pressure statements and provides equal-width ‘Maybe later’ and ‘Upgrade now’ buttons, followed by a saved-free-plan state.
semantic_observation: The language frames upgrading as social conformity and imminent loss, not neutral plan comparison. The explicit deferral path mitigates obstruction but does not remove the manipulative FOMO/persuasive-language condition.

justification: No deceptive condition is observed in the static download page. The source domain, version, size, and action are explicit; there is no disguised external action, consent trap, or hidden payment in the captured bundle.
vision_observation: A single card identifies FileVault Pro and filevaultpro.io, presents a large ‘Download Now’ control, and states 32.4 MB, version, signed installer, and SHA-256 verified.
dom_observation: The download anchor href points to the same filevaultpro.io domain shown in the host/source text; only one state exists and it contains no alternate hidden action.
semantic_observation: The interface semantically identifies the action as downloading a named installer from the displayed host. The claims are not independently verified here, but their presence does not instantiate a deception condition.

justification: The checkout shows a material unexplained $5 discrepancy: listed charges are $59 + $25 + free shipping = $84, while total and button say $89. This conflicts with transparent pricing and supports conflicting-information/hidden-cost concerns.
vision_observation: The final confirmation card shows headphones $59, case $25, free shipping, but total/button $89; the later state confirms the order and repeats the unexplained amount.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly includes those line items, ‘Shipping Free,’ ‘Total $89.00,’ and ‘Place order — $89.00,’ with no tax, service fee, or other $5 node.
semantic_observation: The text promises final confirmation and says the order is non-refundable, but its factual price components do not entail the displayed total. The missing $5 is materially adverse and undisclosed before commitment.

justification: The social-proof claim is specific, temporally qualified, and accompanied by a purchase log that remains stable across states. The static truthful annotation and absence of dynamic inflation support E3’s honest-qualifier escape clause.
vision_observation: The product card shows ‘14 people bought this in the last hour’ alongside a 14-event backend log; after purchase the count/log remain unchanged and the result says ‘Static and truthful.’
dom_observation: Both state blocks preserve the same 14 events, named time entries, $119 price, and purchase-log text; only the CTA changes from Buy now to Order placed.
semantic_observation: The claim has an explicit temporal qualifier and visible supporting event details. It is not presented as an unbounded or rapidly changing number, though backend authenticity cannot be independently checked.

justification: The warranty offer is clearly priced and optional, with equal-weight Add and No thanks controls and a direct confirmation after selection. No preselection, hidden cost, or coercive copy is observed.
vision_observation: The initial card presents ‘Add for $19.99’ and ‘No thanks’ side by side; the later state says ‘Warranty added’ after the paid choice.
dom_observation: The initial DOM has two sibling buttons and explicit two-year/$19.99 disclosure; the later state replaces them with a confirmation message, with no automatic default encoded.
semantic_observation: The copy states the user can decide now or later and uses neutral language. The choice is an ordinary disclosed add-on, not an injected or mandatory purchase.

justification: The footer-moving mechanic is asserted but not demonstrated in the single captured state. It is openly disclosed and a direct ‘Scroll to bottom’ control is visible, so E5 prevents inferring an unobservable obstruction.
vision_observation: The page says the footer moves farther as one scrolls, but the footer and its Privacy Policy/Terms/Contact/Imprint links are already visible; a Scroll to bottom shortcut is present.
dom_observation: The DOM contains a scrollable region, a footer labeled ‘keeps moving…,’ ordinary footer links, and the direct shortcut; no second state records footer displacement.
semantic_observation: The text openly describes the purported moving-target behavior rather than concealing it. Because no transition verifies movement, the mechanism remains unobservable and cannot support a deceptive verdict.

justification: The renewal terms are disclosed directly beside the trial CTA in readable text, so E2 applies. The later state preserves the same disclosure and confirms activation without showing an omitted or altered charge.
vision_observation: The card places bold ‘auto-renews at $49.99/month’ immediately below ‘Start your free 30-day trial’; the later state says Trial activated and retains it.
dom_observation: The DOM includes a bordered disclosure immediately after the CTA stating 30 days, auto-renewal, $49.99/month, and cancellation in settings in both states.
semantic_observation: The user is told the duration, recurring price, automatic renewal, and cancellation location before activation. The commitment is explicit rather than hidden in fine print.

justification: The activity messages have identifiable names/handles and explicit profile references, defeating the ontology’s low-specificity activity condition. No fabricated counter transition, urgency, or coercion is observed.
vision_observation: Each notification names a person or handles, includes ‘IdentityRef,’ and says tap to open profile; the repeated states are visually stable and the result says Profile found.
dom_observation: The DOM contains specific handles such as @sarah.jones, @emily_k, @mark_t, @lena.d, @joe_b, and @david.m plus identity-reference text for each event.
semantic_observation: The social activity is attributed to concrete identities and framed as verifiable, not as vague ‘someone’ activity. The 214 profile-view metric is accompanied by identifiable activity rather than a concealed context.

justification: The flow explicitly mismatches the stated friend-finding purpose with immediate mass marketing invitations: 24 contacts are messaged under the user’s identity with no preview, picker, or confirmation. Friend Spam conditions fire across intent, granular selection, and sender identity.
vision_observation: After granting contact access, the screen reports 24 invitations sent immediately, shows promotional messages under Alex Rivera’s name, and offers no recipient or undo controls.
dom_observation: The state changes Allow access to contacts into Access granted and adds ‘24 invites went out… no preview, no picker, no confirmation,’ plus marketing messages sent via the user’s invite.
semantic_observation: The initial request semantically promises finding existing friends, while the resulting action is unsolicited broadcast marketing. The user’s identity is used as sender without granular consent.

justification: A privacy-sensitive ‘Share my activity data with advertising partners’ checkbox is explicitly marked pre-selected and remains enabled through setup. This fires Bad Defaults/Privacy Zuckering pre-initialized activation, despite clear wording and direct ability to uncheck.
vision_observation: Among 14 settings, the advertising-partner activity-sharing checkbox is checked, highlighted, and marked ‘Pre-selected’; the later saved state retains it.
dom_observation: The DOM form contains the checked advertising-sharing input and a single Finish setup action; the other settings are separate and mostly unchecked.
semantic_observation: The selected setting grants commercial data sharing before affirmative user choice. Its wording is fairly explicit, but preselecting it makes a privacy-invasive consequence easy to accept passively.

justification: The purchase-log claim is bounded by a one-hour window, supported by visible event rows, and unchanged across the purchase transition. No ontology condition proves fabrication from these states.
vision_observation: The product shows 14 events in the last hour with named time entries and a stable count; the CTA changes normally to Order placed and the result says Static and truthful.
dom_observation: The DOM repeats ‘Backend purchase log — last hour,’ 14 events, timestamped entries, and no post-purchase count mutation; only the button becomes disabled/checked out.
semantic_observation: The social-proof assertion is temporally qualified and linked to a concrete log. ‘Static and truthful’ is an in-interface claim, not independent proof, but there is no observed contradiction.

justification: The free trial clearly discloses its duration, recurring price, payment method, and cancellation path, then requests explicit confirmation before charging. This is directly covered by E2 and the real-consent safeguards.
vision_observation: The trial state warns of the $14.99/month charge and offers Cancel trial; at expiry, equal visible Yes-charge and No-cancel controls appear before the final Premium active state.
dom_observation: The DOM progresses from seven-days-remaining and a cancellation button to an expiry confirmation with explicit charge/cancel buttons, then records charge only after confirmation.
semantic_observation: The flow distinguishes trial from paid premium, says nothing is charged until confirmation, and identifies the card and recurring amount. It does not silently convert the user.

justification: Registration is made the dominant checkout path while guest checkout is reduced to a small link and framed as missing benefits. This fires visual hierarchy and confirmshaming conditions, though the guest path remains present so strict forced registration is not proven.
vision_observation: A large purple ‘Create account & check out’ button dominates; ‘Continue without benefits’ is a small underlined control with ‘you’ll miss out’ copy, and the later notice says guest remains available.
dom_observation: The DOM places a full-width primary account button before a small text button labeled Continue without benefits, with discouraging italic text beneath it.
semantic_observation: The guest route is semantically framed as a loss of benefits rather than a neutral checkout alternative. The visible route survives, so the coercion is steering/confirmshaming rather than absolute blocking.

justification: The ad interruption is clearly labeled, the four-second duration is visible, and the interface supplies a visible Skip ad control. E2 and O6 support disclosure and control availability; no hidden exit or forced viewing is observed.
vision_observation: The initial offer states one ad is required; the next state visibly labels the ad, shows 0:04 and progress, and retains a skip affordance in the captured sequence.
dom_observation: The DOM changes the Watch 1 ad button to an Ad panel with a 0:04 timer and progress bar; the copy states the ad requirement before activation.
semantic_observation: The user is told the reward is one common cosmetic sticker with no gameplay effect and that one ad opens it free. The exchange is explicit rather than disguised.

justification: Cancellation technically exists but is intentionally rendered at roughly 1% of the retention action’s prominence. This fires False Hierarchy/visual suppression and obstruction conditions; repeated states show no improved cancellation visibility.
vision_observation: A large bold ‘Keep my subscription — 50% off’ button contrasts with a tiny faint ‘Cancel anyway’ link and a nearly empty Cancel plan bar; the annotation calls out the deliberate 1% prominence.
dom_observation: The DOM gives the keep action a large filled button while cancellation is a small underlined text button with 8px text and only 1% progress-bar width.
semantic_observation: The offer is a retention intervention during cancellation and explicitly directs attention toward staying. The low-salience cancellation route is not neutral even though it is technically available.

justification: The claim is precisely quantified and time-qualified, with an explicit verification control and stable value across states. The verification basis is not independently exposed, but unsupported proof alone does not satisfy a deceptive ontology condition; confidence is capped for that limitation.
vision_observation: ‘128 people viewed this in the last hour’ appears with a Verify claim button; the later state adds Claim verified while preserving the number and qualifier.
dom_observation: The DOM contains the numeric claim, explicit temporal qualifier, Verify claim button, and later verification panel referencing backend analytics without changing the claim.
semantic_observation: The language makes the social-proof statement falsifiable and bounded, unlike an unqualified popularity claim. The interface asserts auditability but does not display the underlying record, so this remains only moderately supported.

justification: The account setup visibly preselects activity-data sharing with advertising partners and saves it without any shown affirmative selection. This directly fires Bad Defaults/Preselection and creates a privacy-commercial consequence by default.
vision_observation: The 14-setting form highlights a checked ‘Share my activity data with advertising partners’ row with a Pre-selected badge; setup is then saved with the same state.
dom_observation: The DOM contains the checked privacy-sensitive checkbox among individually listed preferences and a Finish setup button; the later block adds Setup saved without a recorded opt-in transition.
semantic_observation: The user’s activity data is shared with advertising partners by default, while the user may finish setup passively. Although the label is explicit, the consent state is initialized on rather than requiring opt-in.

justification: The subscription trial is transparent: its recurring charge is disclosed immediately below the CTA in readable text and retained after activation. E2’s disclosure clause prevents a Forced Continuity finding.
vision_observation: CloudNimbus Pro shows a prominent 30-day trial CTA and a bordered, bold $49.99/month auto-renewal disclosure directly beneath it; the later state says Trial activated.
dom_observation: Both state blocks include the exact auto-renewal sentence, monthly amount, and cancellation-in-settings text; only the CTA label changes to Trial activated.
semantic_observation: The copy plainly communicates trial duration, automatic renewal, recurring price, and cancellation location before the user starts. No silent charge or hidden condition is observed.

justification: The reference price is deliberately rendered as a tiny low-contrast strikethrough while the current price dominates. The second state explicitly confirms near-invisibility, firing Reference Pricing visual salience conditions.
vision_observation: PLN 199 is very large and bold; ‘was PLN 299’ is tiny, faint, and struck through. The annotation says the reference baseline can barely be read.
dom_observation: The DOM uses a 20px extra-bold current price versus a 9px accent strikethrough reference price and adds a Faded baseline badge and explanatory notice.
semantic_observation: The old price is the comparison anchor needed to evaluate the deal, yet the interface tells users it is printed ‘somewhere over there’ and visually suppresses it. This is intentional anchoring obfuscation.

justification: The interface shows 27 units in the underlying/displayed stock panel but presents ‘Only 2 left!’ in an alarm-colored pulsing badge, with no stock-feed updates and no change after checkout. Low Stock inventory fabrication and alarm-salience conditions fire.
vision_observation: The product repeatedly shows a red/orange pulsing ‘Only 2 left!’ badge while the supporting panel states 27 units; checkout does not alter either value.
dom_observation: The DOM styles the badge at hsl(12,85%,45%) with animate-pulse and records Refresh stock feed (0x); state s1 retains the same scarcity claim after the Buy now action.
semantic_observation: The shopper-facing quantifier is materially inconsistent with the 27-unit figure and is paired with danger coding to induce immediate purchase. The explanatory note calls the alarm manufactured.

justification: The auto-renewal is disclosed before activation with a concrete price and duration, and the later state confirms the user’s explicit choice. The disclosure is adjacent and readable, so E2 applies.
vision_observation: The trial card states ‘7 days,’ ‘$14.99/mo,’ and that the card will be charged unless canceled; after expiry it offers equal charge/cancel controls and records charge after confirmation.
dom_observation: The DOM progresses from a renewal reminder and Cancel trial to an explicit confirmation block saying nothing is charged until confirm, then Premium active after the charge.
semantic_observation: The text clearly distinguishes reminder, expiration, consent, and charge. It does not silently convert the trial or hide the cancellation route.

justification: The observed bundle is a clearly named, explicitly priced package with listed components and a reversible add-to-cart action. No separate mandatory supplemental item, preselection, or hidden component is demonstrated.
vision_observation: Creator Bundle is shown at $1,199 with Nova camera, 50mm lens, and hard case listed; after adding, a cart summary repeats the price and offers Remove bundle.
dom_observation: Both states contain the same bundle title, component list, and $1199.00 total; s2 adds Added to cart and Remove bundle without inserting another line item.
semantic_observation: The bundle is semantically presented as a bundle, not as a primary item plus an undisclosed supplement. Descriptions remain fully available and the user can reverse the cart addition.

justification: The banner asks the user to pay to unlock Episode 4 while the underlying player simultaneously says Episode 4 is already unlocked and playing. This is an observed semantic contradiction and materially misleading paywall.
vision_observation: The same visual sheet shows ‘Unlock Episode 4: The Heist’ and ‘Unlocked — now playing’ for the same episode, with a visible close X but contradictory pay prompt.
dom_observation: The DOM includes a z-10 paywall overlay naming Episode 4 and a separate s1 status row stating Unlocked — now playing; the close target is only 16px but the contradiction is decisive.
semantic_observation: The two messages cannot both accurately describe the current access state: an already playing episode does not need unlocking. The explicit $3.99/$9.99 offer therefore misdirects the user despite visible pricing.

justification: The upgrade/retention flow is transparent: the trial ends, then the interface requests explicit confirmation with equally clear charge and cancel choices. Renewal and price terms are shown before charging.
vision_observation: States show seven days remaining, a renewal reminder, an expiry confirmation with ‘Yes — charge me $14.99/mo’ and ‘No — cancel my subscription,’ then Premium active only after confirmation.
dom_observation: The DOM contains explicit cancellation before expiry and an expiry prompt stating nothing is charged until confirmation; the final state records a confirmed charge.
semantic_observation: The language names the recurring amount, payment card, cancellation result, and confirmation requirement. There is no forced continuity or concealed automatic charge.

justification: The advertisement is visibly labeled, the waiting period is stated, and a clearly labeled Skip ad control is available. No disguised ad or absent dismissal vector is observed.
vision_observation: The game level-complete state leads to a clearly marked Advertisement with ‘You can skip in 15s’ and visible Skip ad; the final notice calls it neutral framing.
dom_observation: The DOM adds an Advertisement block with explicit ad content, a 15-second skip message, and a Skip ad button, then records Neutral framing.
semantic_observation: The interruption is framed as an ad rather than as game content, and the user is told when/how to leave. The time cost is disclosed and control availability survives.

justification: The trial conversion is not forced: renewal timing and price are disclosed, cancellation is available before expiry and at expiry, and the charge occurs only after an explicit yes action. E2 and explicit-consent safeguards apply.
vision_observation: The later confirmation state says nothing is charged until confirmation and presents equal charge/cancel choices; the final paid state says the charge followed confirmation.
dom_observation: The DOM has a visible Cancel trial button in s0, explicit ‘Yes — charge me’ and ‘No — cancel’ buttons in s1, and Premium active only in s2.
semantic_observation: The semantics clearly separate free trial from paid subscription and identify exact price, payment method, and cancellation outcome. No silent state mutation is observed.

justification: A single unchecked checkbox combines required legal acceptance with optional advertising-partner data sharing and provides no visible separate opt-out. This fires bundled-consent/Privacy Zuckering concern, though the checkbox is not prechecked and the data-sharing wording is explicit.
vision_observation: The registration form shows one unchecked agreement covering Terms, Privacy Policy, and data sharing with advertising partners; Create account is the only primary action.
dom_observation: The DOM has one checkbox whose label joins Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and advertising-partner data sharing, rather than separate controls.
semantic_observation: The text semantically fuses legally necessary account terms with optional commercial data sharing, making acceptance of the latter part of the undifferentiated registration action. No granular refusal is visible.

justification: The interface intentionally suppresses the reference price while emphasizing the current price; the second state explicitly identifies the anchor as nearly unreadable. This fires Reference Pricing visual salience/anchoring conditions.
vision_observation: The current PLN 199 price is dominant while ‘was PLN 299’ is faint, tiny, and struck through; the later note says the reference baseline is faded to near-invisibility.
dom_observation: The current price is rendered at 20px extra-bold while the reference price is 9px accent line-through, and the DOM adds a Faded baseline annotation.
semantic_observation: The previous price supplies the user’s value anchor but is deliberately made difficult to read. The copy itself acknowledges that the baseline is somewhere over there, confirming concealment rather than ordinary hierarchy.

justification: The low-stock claim is directly contradicted by the displayed 27-unit quantity and remains unchanged after checkout with zero feed refreshes. Red pulsing alarm styling compounds the observed fabricated-scarcity condition.
vision_observation: A hiking backpack card repeatedly shows ‘Only 2 left!’ in a warm alarm badge, while the accompanying measurement panel shows 27 units; Buy now becomes Checked out without stock movement.
dom_observation: The badge uses animate-pulse and hsl(12,85%,45%), while the DOM exposes ‘Refresh stock feed (0x)’ and retains the two-unit claim across states.
semantic_observation: The interface presents a panic-inducing scarcity quantifier despite a much larger inventory figure and no transaction-linked change. The final text explicitly calls the alarm manufactured.

justification: The app requests unrelated location permission for a camera function and blocks the camera after refusal. The observed purpose-permission mismatch, coercive gating, and refusal penalty fire Granting and Interaction/permission manipulation conditions.
vision_observation: SnapCam claims to take a front-camera photo but requests location; after ‘Not now,’ it says Camera unavailable and that the shutter stays blocked until Allow.
dom_observation: The DOM keeps a Location: off status and changes the notice to ‘Camera unavailable’ while retaining Not now and Allow location; the text explicitly says the shutter stays blocked until Allow.
semantic_observation: The advertised utility is camera capture, whereas the requested permission is geographic location. The flow presents location as necessary without a functional explanation and punishes refusal by blocking the core feature.
